name: picoscope-fake
experiment:
# Block-mode oscilloscope capture through the picoscope plugin.
#
# This build has NO real PicoScope driver (see docs/adr/0024-picoscope.md): it
# runs against the plugin's SYNTHETIC scope, so every waveform is generated, not
# measured. Real PicoScope validation is PENDING.
#
#   HWLAB_PICOSCOPE_FAKE=1 hwlab run --yes examples/picoscope-fake.yaml
#   hwlab waveform measure latest --source scope --channel A
#
# Signals on the synthetic scope: A 1 kHz square 0..3.3 V (rise 2 us, fall 4 us),
# B 10 kHz sine +-1 V, C DC 1.2 V, D 50 Hz sine +-15 V (overflows ranges <= 10 V).
name: picoscope-fake
duration: 3s

devices:
  scope:
    plugin: picoscope
    device: fake-ps
    channels: [A, B]
    range_v: 5
    sample_rate_hz: 2000000
    samples: 8000
    pre_trigger: 0.1
    trigger_source: A
    trigger_level_v: 1.65
    trigger_slope: rising

steps:
  - {name: info,    at: 100ms, device: scope, call: Oscilloscope.info}
  - {name: measure, at: 1s,    device: scope, call: Oscilloscope.measure, args: {channel: A}}
  - {name: shape,   at: 1100ms, device: scope, call: Oscilloscope.waveform, args: {channel: B, points: 40}}

plots:
  - name: scope
    title: Synthetic oscilloscope capture
    format: svg

clock.source: host clock (synthetic instrument: no real acquisition)
clock.note: SYNTHETIC oscilloscope; times only order the events
